title: pfs — full 12-step run: 'Connection for loved ones' (customer brief, training numbers)

beats.speaker: human
beats.text: Setting up the environment and running a full pass of the 'Product Factory Strategist' agent on the customer brief 'Connection for loved ones and own devices'. From installation to the final package — all twelve steps.

beats.out: environment: Python 3.12 ✓ · ffmpeg ✓ · say ✓ · fonts ✓ · hooks ✓ · {{tests}} tests green

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: All the machinery runs on the Python standard library: registries, hooks, quote verification. No external APIs, CLI cost is zero dollars. Before starting, I check which methodology cards exist in the knowledge base.

beats.out: {{kb_cards}} cards: customers · JTBD · market size · MVP and pilots · cannibalization · unit economics · risks · monetization

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: A project is created with one command. Task state lives in project files, not in chat memory — that is the key to resuming after a break.

beats.cmd: python3 -m tools.pfs new 'Connection for loved ones and own devices' 'Customer brief: who to help first, what to change, a one-year plan, a third-year benchmark'
beats.out: Project created. Active. Next step: intake

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: The router suggests the scenario: go-to-market. Step maps: customers, JTBD, market size, MVP pilots. Model plan: deep for options and strategy, fast for classification and extraction.

beats.out: scenario: go-to-market · maps: customers, JTBD, market size, MVP pilots · models: deep×3, fast×4 · confidence: high

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Step one is intake. The pause is mandatory: a human turns the brief into working fields. The agent waits until the lead confirms the task.

beats.speaker: human
beats.text: Brief from the customer: 'Connection for loved ones and own devices'. Who to help first? What to change? A one-year plan, a third-year benchmark. Decisions: end of Q1 — pilot? End of Q2 — expand?

beats.out: 2 questions: service audience boundaries? · which outage data can be used? → answers written to 00_brief

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: The brief becomes document 00_brief: the question, two decisions Q1 and Q2, the comparison axis — gross profit and active groups. Success thresholds are written before the data — more honest than fitting them afterwards.

beats.out: intake: done · next step: sources

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Step two is sources. Rule number one: every material claim gets a source. Registering the brief: the file is fetched, cleaned, deduplicated by checksum.

beats.out: S001 [public/text] Brief 'Connection for loved ones' · sources/raw/brief.md · sha256 recorded

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: One necessary source: a training market, every number comes from the assignment. Competitors are the customer's own workarounds from the brief, no real brands. Quote checking is on: every claim stores a verbatim quote.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Step three is research. The plan is built not from data but from questions that can change the decision. Seven questions; for each — where the answer comes from and what happens if it differs.

beats.out: Step 3/12 research · in_progress

beats.cmd: pfs claim add 'Year-one target: gross profit 282M, estimate 275M' --kind fact --source S001 --grade A
beats.out: C001 [fact · A · S001] with a quote from the brief

beats.cmd: pfs claim add 'Decision boundary: 12,000 extra paid months × 500 RUB = +6M' --kind fact --source S001 --grade A
beats.out: C003 [fact · A · S001]

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: I register ten facts C001–C010 in batches: plan and estimate, the 500-ruble rate per extra paid month, markets of 100 and 40 thousand households, consent rights, three person-months of resources.

beats.out: C001–C010 · kind=fact · grade=A · source=S001 · each with a verbatim quote

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: The claim type is always explicit: fact, assumption, hypothesis, forecast, inference. The agent's own conclusion is never written as a fact: it is no stronger than its weakest critical input. Synthetic data cannot become evidence — more on that next.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: To test behavioral hypotheses — two AI respondents: a family organizer and a router owner. First an interview guide, then transcripts into a separate folder marked as synthetic.

beats.out: 12-question guide → interviews/guide-organizer.md
S002 [synthetic] · family organizer · hypotheses only
S003 [synthetic] · router owner · hypotheses only

beats.cmd: pfs claim add 'They would enable warnings if only the remaining balance is visible' --kind hypothesis --source S002
beats.out: C019 [hypothesis · synthetic] — type enforced

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Hypotheses C019 and C020: they would enable warnings if only the remaining balance is visible; monetization through retention. The fact checker blocks synthetic data: AI answers do not prove demand.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Economics — a reproducible script, not a number from thin air. The decision boundary from the brief: with no new spend, the goal of plus six million equals twelve thousand extra paid months at 500 rubles.

beats.out: boundary: {{boundary_months}} months × RUB 500 = +6M · scenarios: +6.75 / +5.5 / +4.5 / +1.5 / −1.5 / −3.5M

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Target scenario: five and a half thousand numbers for three months minus 1.5 million of costs — plus 6.75 million, total {{target_mln}} million against a goal of at least 285. Adverse — 280.5; the zero scenario — 277.5.

beats.out: affects: inference C021 → 03_options.md → decision D001

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Steps four and five — the situation picture. What we know: facts C001–C010 from the brief. What we do not know: outage cause frequencies are not given — assumptions C011 and C012 are recorded with a pilot-data check plan.

beats.out: 3 gaps: outage cause frequencies · balance forecast accuracy · organizer behavior on 'confirm payment'

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: A separate pass — the family dashboard mockup: a ux-review across ten heuristics, only what is visible in the picture, source S004. No speculation about what the mockup does not show.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: The contradiction from the brief is stated honestly: depletion data exists, warnings do not — so the problem is not the data. Segments S1–S3: elderly parents, their adult children, owners of their own devices.

beats.out: 02_situation.md: 0 errors · every number tagged [C###]/[S###]

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Step six — options. The process requires at least three materially different ones, including boring choices. Here there are five: A — status quo, B — warnings before the outage, C — family dashboard, D — routers first, E — shut down.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Each option faces strong objections, not straw men. A loses six million against the goal. C costs four to five person-months with an unmeasured effect. D bets on hardware before demand is tested.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Red team — an independent subagent tasked with breaking the recommendation. Result: twenty hits — fifteen objections and five hidden assumptions. Verdict: needs rework before the pilot.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: The key catch: the organizer sees a 'confirm payment' prompt — while consent rights say the payer confirms payments, not a relative. Without rework the recommendation would violate rights.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: The rework is built into thresholds: reminders go to the payer, three granular consents instead of one, incremental payments with a ninety-day window. Red team objections are not discarded — they become conditions.

beats.cmd: pfs ask 'Which option do you approve for the pilot?' --options 'A,B,C,D,E'
beats.out: question recorded · choice pause · waiting for the lead

beats.speaker: human
beats.text: I approve option B — warnings before the outage. Pilot in Q1, the expansion decision follows the results.

beats.out: answer recorded · choice: done · next step: strategy

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: The pause is closed by the lead. Step eight — product and communication strategies, consistent with each other. Product: the warning arrives before the outage, one button to act, no dashboard visit required.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Both strategies carry a 'promise — what confirms it in the product' table. Conscious exclusions are written: no geolocation, no message reading, free within the plan. A promise without product proof is a review defect.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Step nine — the validation plan with pre-registration: thresholds written before the data. Primary metric — extra paid months per group, intention-to-treat. A/B across six hundred family groups.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Customer threshold: minus three percentage points of cutoff-driven restrictions — from twelve to nine percent. Stop metrics: consent withdrawals above fifteen percent, repeat charges at zero, forecast accuracy at least eighty percent.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: The threshold is read carefully: if the range is compatible with both benefit and zero, the benefit conclusion is not sufficient and observation is extended. That rule comes from the brief, not from the agent.

beats.out: 0 errors · {{claims_total}} claims: {{c_fact}} facts, {{c_assumption}} assumptions, {{c_hyp}} hypotheses, {{c_inf}} inferences

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Step ten — review. Independent rubric-based audit scored forty-six out of sixty: five defects. All fixed — the red team hit count, scenario desync, the target scenario taken from the decision boundary, the timeline, consent thresholds.

beats.out: verdict recorded · registry edits after lock require a fresh review
counted in project cost · 15 human minutes

beats.speaker: human
beats.text: Approving the decision: pilot of six hundred groups, review at the end of Q2.

beats.cmd: pfs decision add --title 'Warning pilot' --decision 'option B, 600 groups, ITT' --owner CPO --grounds C013,C016,C017,C003,C015,C027 --metric '−3 p.p. @2027-06-30' --review 2027-04-30 --commitment 'support cost estimate|product|before pilot'
beats.out: {{decision_id}} accepted · metrics and review triggers recorded

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: The decision is not abandoned: commitments with deadlines — support cost estimate, pre-registration, consent rights, payment idempotency. Monitoring is open, review on April 30, 2027.

beats.speaker: human
beats.text: (break — opening a fresh chat the next day)

beats.out: Project: Connection for loved ones · Step 12/12 monitoring · decision {{decision_id}} · commitments 4 · review 2027-04-30

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Resuming after a break took one command: state lives in files, not in chat memory. Sources and claims are not duplicated — the tool returns existing identifiers.

beats.out: Assembled {{artifacts}} artifacts: REPORT.md/docx · SIX_PAGER RU/EN · DOCX · deck · 4 formula-driven Excel workbooks

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: And the main artifact for the jury: BRIEF_RESPONSE — one document in five parts, as the brief requires. Part one — customers and the problem. Part two — the case walkthrough with situation reconstruction.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Part three — the offer and the journey of both roles, acquisition and connection forecast. Part four — benefit of minus three points and profit: the boundary of {{boundary_months}} months at 500 rubles, target scenario {{target_mln}} million.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Part five — the choice among five options, the plan by quarters, the forecast for all five lines, resources, risks and one concrete request. Calculations sit next to decisions, not in a hundred-page appendix.

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Transparency throughout: what was done — in the log; what conclusions rest on — C### tags back to S### sources; what new information would change — via the impact command; what it cost — via the cost command.

beats.out: CLI part: $0.00 · all machinery on stdlib Python · {{tests}} tests green

beats.speaker: pfs
beats.text: Full-run summary: every number carries a source tag, synthetic stays hypothesis-only, the red team attacked its own recommendation, the decision ships with commitments and a review date. Training numbers, real process.
